When a CSV file ends with an empty line (a trailing newline), text.split('
') creates an empty string at the end of the lines array. Although parser.ts attempts to pop a single empty line from the end with 'if (lines.length > 0 && lines[lines.length - 1] === '') lines.pop()', if the file ends with multiple newlines or if there are blank lines at the end of the file, or if the logic pops only one and the loop still processes it or encounters an empty line, wait: let's look closer. In sample = ["Date,Amount,Description", "2026-03-01,-4.20,Coffee", "2026-03-02,1500.00,Salary", ""].join("
"), lines has length 4: ['Date,Amount,Description', '2026-03-01,-4.20,Coffee', '2026-03-02,1500.00,Salary', '']. lines.pop() removes the last '' element, leaving 3 lines (header + 2 rows). But what if there are trailing newlines or a blank line at the end resulting in an empty field/line or if lines[index] is empty? Wait, if a statement ends with an empty line, text.split('
') produces a trailing empty string, which lines.pop() removes. BUT what if there are *multiple* trailing empty lines or an empty line at the end that isn't popped because of carriage returns (
)? On Windows, 
 splitting leaves  at the end of lines, so lines[lines.length - 1] is "", not "", or split('
') leaves empty lines with . Let's check how lines are split or handled.
result.label: bug

input.title: Fix CSV parser handling of trailing newlines and CRLF line endings
input.body:
File: src/ingest/parser.ts

Handle Windows line endings (CRLF) and multiple trailing blank lines when parsing CSV files, ensuring trailing carriage returns and empty lines do not cause parsing errors or empty rows.
